key_insight: Plastic shear on FCC slip systems is controlled mainly by the availability of long dislocation links, whose length distribution and threshold-like velocity together produce the observed exponential stress dependence.
engineering_relevance: This gives a physics-based flow rule that can improve crystal plasticity models by predicting slip activity from dislocation microstructure rather than stress alone.
method: Integrate shear-rate contributions from dislocation links over link length on each slip system.
Use a generalized Orowan equation linking link density n_i(l) and average link velocity v_i(l) to shear rate.
Fit a shared velocity law v(τ_i,l) across slip systems while capturing inter-system effects through n_i(l).
evidence_signal: The model reproduces discrete dislocation dynamics shear-rate data for all 12 FCC slip systems across 99 loading orientations.
watch_item: The velocity law is inferred from DDD data and may need recalibration when microstructure, slip interactions, or loading conditions fall outside the studied FCC single-crystal setting.
paper_title: Plastic Flow Rule Based on Dislocation Link Velocity
